text: {"score":3,"justification":"The numbers and the cautious 'inconclusive' leaning are grounded in the card and tool outputs. The cited examples are weak, though, and the narrative has an internal contradiction and some unsupported wording. An investigator would have to redo some of the analysis.","problems":["Headline says '26% of notes describe data review with no tests on the claim', but the card shows 5 of 15 moderate-plus data notes (33%). The 26% is 5 of 19 charts, so the denominator is mislabeled and misleading.","Rationale says 'Notes claim data review that the claims do not show, which weakens the documentation'. This is a conclusion stated too firmly from 5 notes, while the leaning is inconclusive and 0 charts were below billed.","The 'against 9% for the comparison providers' figure matches the card's all-provider 99215 rate of 0.087. It is not explained that this comparison rests on only 4 documented 99215 claims.","Only two example claims are cited, both low-complexity 99215s. No claim with the data-without-tests issue is cited, and no documented claim is cited, so the cited claims do not support the documentation point. The card offers 25 low-complexity examples, and the high-complexity 99215s are not used for contrast.","The summary is internally mixed: it reports strong billing outliers (5.16x expected, z 2.93) but leans inconclusive. It does not explain that the inconclusive leaning comes from thin documentation.","Next steps are generic: 'larger sample' has no size, and 'Re-screen' is vague. They don't name specific claims to request, and they omit the record-exchange problems (SCOPE_UNCLEAR, MISSING_VISITS, 11 charts missing). 'A coder should re-score the notes' is also not tied to specific claims.","'z_adj 7.4' is a stray, unexplained duplicate of the risk-adjusted score."]}
